periods.why: cycle 24 rising: spots at higher latitudes
cycle 24 declining: spots near the equator (AR 2673)

reason: Rate falling linearly with |φ| and Differential rotation (sin² φ) forecast equally well (BIC within 10).

laws.title: Differential rotation (sin² φ and sin⁴ φ)

outcome.headline: The Sun turns faster at its equator: 14.46 + (-3.11) sin² φ degrees per day (sidereal), from 119 sunspots in real SDO images, matching the published sunspot profile. Regions came back on the east limb a median 1.5 days from the forecast (7 returns).
outcome.action: Use the return dates to plan observations of regions due back on the east limb.

checked_against.name: sidereal rate at 15° latitude (deg/day)
checked_against.source: Allen's Astrophysical Quantities (sunspot rotation, as in sunpy); NOAA SWPC region summaries

outcome.confidence: A = 14.46 ± 0.02, B = -3.11 ± 0.18 °/day; spots scatter by 0.58 °/day about the law (their own motions)

return_bias.candidates: spot proper motion relative to the surface; regions decaying and re-forming further east
